tcgshop.fact.1: Every great collection starts like the Pokédex: with number 001, Bulbasaur.
tcgshop.fact.4: Number 004 matches Charmander. May your collection burn bright!
tcgshop.fact.7: Number 007 matches Squirtle. Your collection is starting to make waves.
tcgshop.fact.10: Number 010 matches Caterpie, the first Pokémon Ash caught in the anime.
tcgshop.fact.25: Number 025 matches Pikachu, the most famous Pokémon in the world!
tcgshop.fact.39: Number 039 matches Jigglypuff. It would sing with joy... even if everyone fell asleep.
tcgshop.fact.52: Number 052 matches Meowth. With this many cards, that's quite a Pay Day!
tcgshop.fact.60: 60 cards is exactly the size of a standard Pokémon TCG deck.
tcgshop.fact.94: Number 094 matches Gengar, who is surely peeking at your collection from your shadow.
tcgshop.fact.100: Number 100 matches Voltorb. Careful, don't explode with excitement.
tcgshop.fact.102: 102 cards: the same number as the original 1999 Base Set.
tcgshop.fact.108: Number 108 matches Lickitung... and Spiritomb is made of 108 spirits.
tcgshop.fact.129: Number 129 matches Magikarp. Everyone underestimates it until it evolves. Like your collection.
tcgshop.fact.133: Number 133 matches Eevee: as many evolutions as ways to sort a binder.
tcgshop.fact.143: Number 143 matches Snorlax, blocking the road... to your next pack.
tcgshop.fact.150: Number 150 matches Mewtwo, the Pokémon created by science.
tcgshop.fact.151: 151! The same as the original Kanto Pokédex, which ends with Mew.
tcgshop.fact.197: Number 197 matches Umbreon, star of some of the most expensive modern cards.
tcgshop.fact.249: Number 249 matches Lugia, guardian of the seas.
tcgshop.fact.250: Number 250 matches Ho-Oh: they say whoever sees it finds eternal happiness.
tcgshop.fact.251: Number 251 matches Celebi, who closes the Johto Pokédex. Your collection travels through time.
tcgshop.fact.282: Number 282 matches Gardevoir, willing to protect its trainer with its life.
tcgshop.fact.384: Number 384 matches Rayquaza, lord of the skies.
tcgshop.fact.386: Number 386 matches Deoxys, who closes the Hoenn Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.448: Number 448 matches Lucario, who can sense the aura... of rare cards.
tcgshop.fact.493: Number 493 matches Arceus, who according to myth created the universe.
tcgshop.fact.500: Half a thousand different cards! Emboar, number 500, celebrates big.
tcgshop.fact.570: Number 570 matches Zorua, who could pass for any of your cards.
tcgshop.fact.649: Number 649 matches Genesect, who closes the Unova Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.658: Number 658 matches Greninja, the ninja master of Kalos.
tcgshop.fact.700: Number 700 matches Sylveon, the Fairy-type Eeveelution.
tcgshop.fact.721: Number 721 matches Volcanion, who closes the Kalos Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.778: Number 778 matches Mimikyu, who just wants to be loved... like your common cards.
tcgshop.fact.809: Number 809 matches Melmetal, who closes the Alola Pokédex (and came from Pokémon GO).
tcgshop.fact.888: Number 888 matches Zacian. Triple eight, a lucky number!
tcgshop.fact.898: Number 898 matches Calyrex, who closes the Galar Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.905: Number 905 matches Enamorus, the last Pokémon discovered in Hisui.
tcgshop.fact.999: Number 999 matches Gimmighoul. You'd need 999 of its coins to evolve it.
tcgshop.fact.1000: 1,000 different cards! Gholdengo, number 1000, is made of 1,000 coins. You, of 1,000 cards.
tcgshop.fact.1025: Number 1025 matches Pecharunt, the last Pokémon in the National Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.1500: 1,500 cards. If each were a Gimmighoul coin, you could evolve one and a half.
tcgshop.fact.1996: 1996: the year Pokémon was born with Red and Green, on February 27th.
tcgshop.fact.1999: 1999: the year the Pokémon TCG arrived in English with Base Set.
tcgshop.fact.2500: 2,500 different cards. Some real shops have less variety than your binder.
tcgshop.fact.3000: 3,000 different cards. Lined up, they'd stretch over 260 meters.
tcgshop.fact.4000: 4,000 different cards. You know more artworks than many Pokémon Professors.
tcgshop.fact.5000: 5,000 different cards. Your collection has a history of its own.
tcgshop.fact.6000: 6,000 different cards. Professor Oak would want to see your binder.
tcgshop.fact.7000: 7,000 different cards. Few trainers have come this far.
tcgshop.fact.8000: 8,000 different cards. This isn't a collection anymore: it's a museum.

tcgshop.league.rules:
COMPETITIVE TCG MODE

• Deck of up to 20 cards from your collection (max 2 copies, at least 6 Pokémon, at most 6 Items). If you don't save one, it's built from your best cards.
• Every Pokémon has HP, a type and two attacks based on its species and rarity. Non-Pokémon cards are Items: Potion, Research, Switch or Extra Energy.
• You start with 5 cards and your strongest Pokémon as Active. Each turn draw 1, bench Pokémon (max 3), use Items, attach 1 energy and retreat by paying its cost.
• Attacking ends your turn. If the attacker's type is super effective against the defender, it deals +20.
• A knockout scores 1 point (2 for ex: Double Rare or higher). First to 3, or leaving the rival without Pokémon, wins.
• League matches between players: win or lose ELO points and climb ranks (Bronze → Master). Against the house: a CobbleDollars prize.

tcgshop.ptcg.rules:
REAL POKÉMON TCG

Matches use the twinleaf.gg engine (open source, MIT licence) with the official rules and each card's real effects: 60-card decks, 6 prizes, evolution, typed Energy, weakness/resistance, special conditions, Supporters, Stadiums and Tools.

• Play: from the phone (TCG League → Play) against the AI on 4 levels, League vs AI (points at stake) or find an online opponent. Challenge another player from the Cobblemon wheel (“TCG challenge”) or with /tcgduel <player>. Also at a Play Table.
• League matches (vs the AI or players) give rank points; losing them costs a little money. The Veteran and Champion AIs play top meta decks.
• Your deck is checked before every match: 60 cards, max 4 per name, 1 ACE SPEC, 1 Radiant, banned combos and that you own the copies.
• At the table: click any card to zoom in with its attacks and abilities (attack, use abilities or retreat from there). Drag cards from your hand onto their glowing target; drag your Active onto the Bench to retreat.
• ? (S key) = AI hint · ☰ (L key) = detailed log and concede · Space = end turn · Tab = look at the board during a choice.
